fatal_errors: The proposed Ti-induced coherent TiC precipitation intervention is not supported by any cited evidence; none establishes that 2–5 at.% Ti plus trace carbon produces coherent, dispersed TiC in an additively manufactured W-based RHEA.
The cited studies do not demonstrate the asserted causal link between coherent TiC interfaces, helium trapping, enhanced defect recombination, and reduced helium-bubble growth.
The proposal does not reconstruct the demonstrated V-dependent W–Ta intervention, chemical short-range-order mechanism, or Kr-ion irradiation regime.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad plasma-facing RHEA problem and offers a controlled comparison with measurable irradiation and mechanical outcomes. It is also reasonably falsifiable through TEM and mechanical testing. However, it diverges almost completely from the target: it substitutes Ti/TiC precipitation in an additively manufactured W–Ta–Cr–V alloy under helium irradiation for minor V additions to nanocrystalline sputtered W–Ta films under 1 MeV Kr irradiation. The target mechanism concerns V-dependent chemical short-range order, reduced interstitial mobility, vacancy–interstitial recombination, and suppression of segregation and void formation. The generated mechanism instead relies on unverified coherent TiC sinks. E1 supports coherent precipitates as a strength–ductility strategy but not TiC formation or radiation tolerance; E3 supports studying additively manufactured RHEAs under helium irradiation but not the proposed intervention; E2 supplies only general motivation. Thus this is a novel and testable idea, but its central materials state and causal rationale are insufficiently evidenced.
